common: Ice N' Roses Ivory Blush Hellebore
latin: Helleborus × glandorfensis 'HG 1416' (HGC ICE N' ROSES IVORY BLUSH)
hardinessNote: Very hardy in UK gardens, potentially tolerating temperatures below -20°C. Protect container roots from prolonged severe frost.
visual: Abundant ivory-white winter blooms · striking dark flower stems · lush evergreen foliage
pest: Slugs, snails, aphids; occasional hellebore leaf spot
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained; neutral to alkaline
soilWarning: Avoid waterlogged ground and prolonged drought, especially in full sun.
water: Water regularly while establishing. Maintain moderate, even moisture during active growth and flowering. Established plants tolerate short dry periods, but containers need more frequent watering.
prune: Remove damaged, diseased or ageing foliage in late winter. Cut away spent flower stems after flowering if desired. Avoid removing healthy evergreen leaves unnecessarily.
toxicity: Toxic if eaten by humans, cats and dogs. Sap may irritate skin; wear gloves when handling.
cvs: HGC Ice N' Roses Ivory Blush; breeder denomination 'HG 1416'
resilience: Robust, long-lived, cold-hardy evergreen perennial. Tolerates sun and partial shade, with good general disease resistance when drainage and airflow are adequate.
uses: Winter borders, woodland edges, entrance planters, patio containers, underplanting shrubs, early pollinator planting
foliage: Evergreen; leathery, divided, deep-green leaves forming a dense clump
pollination: Insect-pollinated; winter and early-spring flowers can provide nectar and pollen for active bees.
uncertain: H7 hardiness is reported by a UK nursery for this cultivar; an independent RHS cultivar-specific rating was not located.
Sunlight ratings and growth-speed score are horticultural estimates rather than cultivar-specific measurements.
